answer: When a new AI joins the lagoon, it must submit a PoW that hashes the current network pulse plus a random nonce; the required hash difficulty scales as k·(ΔR)^2 where ΔR is the increase in registration rate over the last block, so a sudden surge of identities inflates the work superlinearly. Each applicant locks an anchor token equal to the work‑cost C = k·(ΔR)^2 units, which is burned if the proof fails. An attacker therefore pays a quadratic cost C per fake identity and must wait the block interval for the pulse to update before launching the next attempt.
